title: The Millers' summer of lawsuits: HO liability and endorsements
summary: One Grand Rapids summer: Coverages E and F, the Section II extras, boats Up North, the outline's endorsements, and Michigan's innocent co-insured rule.
objectives: Tell Coverage E from Coverage F, and know the Section II additional coverages
Apply the HO-3 watercraft rules and know when the Watercraft endorsement is needed
Match each selected endorsement to the gap it fills
Explain Michigan's innocent co-insured rule for a fire loss

scenes.title: The Millers' summer of lawsuits
scenes.subtitle: HO-3 Section II liability and the exam's endorsements (2011 ISO HO-3, HO 00 03 05 11)

beats.text: July in Grand Rapids. The Millers throw a backyard barbecue, insured by their 2011 HO-3.
beats.say: July in Grand Rapids. The Millers throw a backyard barbecue, insured by their twenty eleven H O three.

beats.text: By Labor Day, Sam will be sued. Twice. Welcome to Section II: liability. Then come the homeowners endorsements on the exam outline.
beats.say: By Labor Day, Sam will be sued. Twice. Welcome to Section two: liability. Then come the homeowners endorsements on the exam outline.

scenes.title: A friend's fall: Coverage F
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. II Coverage F; ISO HO Manual Table 301 (RIJRA); memory hook mn_prop-14
scenes.plain: Pays other people's medical bills, like a guest hurt at your place, for expenses incurred within 3 years of the accident.
scenes.example: Ed from next door trips on the Millers' sidewalk at the barbecue and sprains his wrist. Coverage F pays his doctor bills.
scenes.exam: Never for you or regular residents of your household, except residence employees. Manual minimum: $1,000 per person.

beats.text: First, Ed from next door trips on the Millers' sidewalk.
beats.say: First, Ed from next door trips on the Millers' sidewalk.

beats.text: Ouch! My wrist!
beats.say: Ouch! My wrist!

beats.text: Coverage F, Medical Payments to Others, pays other people's medical bills, like a guest hurt at your place. It pays for expenses incurred within 3 years of the accident.
beats.say: Coverage F, Medical Payments to Others, pays other people's medical bills, like a guest hurt at your place. It pays for expenses incurred within three years of the accident.

beats.text: Ed sprained his wrist at the Millers' barbecue. So F pays his doctor bills. F: a friend's fall.
beats.say: Ed sprained his wrist at the Millers' barbecue. So F pays his doctor bills. F: a friend's fall.

beats.text: Watch out: never for you or regular residents of your household, except residence employees. Manual minimum: $1,000 per person.
beats.say: Watch out: never for you or regular residents of your household, except residence employees. Manual minimum: one thousand dollars per person.

scenes.title: Sam's call: whose bills go to Coverage F?
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. II Coverage F; question prop-052
scenes.ask: Whose bills should Sam send to F?

draw.text: Their son, 9, lives at home: sprained ankle

beats.text: More bad luck: Sam burns his hand at the grill. Their 9-year-old son, who lives with them, sprains an ankle on the trampoline. Whose bills go to F?
beats.say: More bad luck: Sam burns his hand at the grill. Their nine year old son, who lives with them, sprains an ankle on the trampoline. Whose bills go to F?

options.label: Sam's own burned hand
options.fail: Coverage F is medical payments to others. It never pays for you or regular residents of your household (residence employees aside).

beats.text: But it's my policy!
beats.say: But it's my policy!

beats.text: Exactly: medical payments to others. Never to you.
beats.say: Exactly: medical payments to others. Never to you.

options.label: Their son's sprained ankle
options.fail: Their son is a regular resident of the household. F doesn't pay for household residents, except residence employees.

beats.text: Denied. He's a regular resident of their household.
beats.say: Denied. He's a regular resident of their household.

options.label: Ed's sprained wrist
options.win: Ed is a guest, hurt at the Millers' place with permission. F pays his medical bills incurred within 3 years of the accident.

beats.text: Ed is a guest, so F pays. He even sends a thank-you card. For now.
beats.say: Ed is a guest, so F pays. He even sends a thank-you card. For now.

reveal.text: F is for others, like guests: never you or your household, except residence employees.
reveal.say: F is for others, like guests: never you or your household, except residence employees.

scenes.title: Excuse me, you're being sued: Coverage E
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. II Coverage E; ISO HO Manual Table 301 (RIJRA); question prop-053; memory hook mn_prop-14
scenes.plain: Pays damages you're legally liable for because of bodily injury or property damage, and pays for your defense.
scenes.example: A month later, Ed sues Sam, blaming a cracked sidewalk for his fall. Sam's insurer defends him and pays damages he owes, up to the limit.
scenes.exam: Defends even if the suit is groundless, false or fraudulent, until the limit is used up by a judgment or settlement. Manual minimum: $100,000.

beats.text: A month later, Ed sues Sam over the fall. Excuse me, you're being sued! That's Coverage E, Personal Liability.
beats.say: A month later, Ed sues Sam over the fall. Excuse me, you're being sued! That's Coverage E, Personal Liability.

beats.text: It pays damages Sam is legally liable for because of bodily injury or property damage, plus his defense. Ed blames a cracked sidewalk for his fall. Sam's insurer defends him and pays damages he owes, up to the limit.
beats.say: It pays damages Sam is legally liable for because of bodily injury or property damage, plus his defense. Ed blames a cracked sidewalk for his fall. Sam's insurer defends him and pays damages he owes, up to the limit.

beats.text: It defends even groundless, false or fraudulent suits, until a judgment or settlement uses up the limit. Manual minimum: $100,000.
beats.say: It defends even groundless, false or fraudulent suits, until a judgment or settlement uses up the limit. Manual minimum: one hundred thousand dollars.

scenes.title: Four extras, paid on top of the limits
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. II Additional Coverages A–D; question prop-055; memory hook mn_prop-19

draw.text: Claim expenses: lost pay helping the defense, up to $250 a day
Some catches: on purpose by an insured 13 or older; property an insured owns; damage from business or motor vehicles

beats.text: Under the 2011 form, Section II also pays four extras, on top of the limits.
beats.say: Under the twenty eleven form, Section two also pays four extras, on top of the limits.

beats.text: Claim expenses: defense costs, and Sam's lost pay up to $250 a day for time helping with the defense. Plus first aid to others.
beats.say: Claim expenses: defense costs, and Sam's lost pay up to two hundred fifty dollars a day for time helping with the defense. Plus first aid to others.

beats.text: Damage to property of others: up to $1,000 at replacement cost. Loss assessment: $1,000.
beats.say: Damage to property of others: up to one thousand dollars at replacement cost. Loss assessment: one thousand dollars.

beats.text: Some catches: property of others won't pay if an insured 13 or older did it on purpose, or for property an insured owns. Nor for damage from business or motor vehicles.
beats.say: Some catches: property of others won't pay if an insured thirteen or older did it on purpose, or for property an insured owns. Nor for damage from business or motor vehicles.

scenes.title: Damage to property of others: paid or not?
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. II Add'l Cov. C; question prop-055; memory hook mn_prop-19

cards.text: Their 9-year-old drops Ed's borrowed laptop. Crack!
cards.why: An accident to someone else's property: paid up to $1,000, at replacement cost.

cards.text: Their 15-year-old smashes Ed's mailbox on purpose.
cards.why: Intentional damage by an insured 13 or older isn't covered.

cards.text: Sam accidentally cracks his own snowblower.
cards.why: Property owned by an insured isn't covered.

cards.text: Their 9-year-old breaks Ed's window on purpose.
cards.why: 13 or older AND intentional. A 9-year-old's intentional damage can be paid.

cards.text: Their 15-year-old trips and dents Ed's borrowed ladder.
cards.why: Not on purpose, so age doesn't matter. An accident by a 15-year-old is paid.

cards.text: Sam's home business: he breaks a customer's drill.
cards.why: Business-related damage isn't covered by Damage to Property of Others.

beats.text: Your turn. Does property of others pay? Swipe through the Millers' summer.
beats.say: Your turn. Does property of others pay? Swipe through the Millers' summer.

reveal.text: The trap: 13 or older AND on purpose. An insured's own property never counts, and neither does business damage.
reveal.say: The trap: thirteen or older AND on purpose. An insured's own property never counts, and neither does business damage.

scenes.title: Sam's call: the boat Up North
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. II Excl. B.2; PF&M 2014 (HO 24 75); questions prop-054, prop-gap-16, prop-gap-17; hook mn_prop-20

draw.text: 40 hp. Bought 2 years before this policy period.
What if I hurt someone out there?

beats.text: August, Up North on Houghton Lake. Sam's boat has a 40-horsepower outboard, bought 2 years before this policy period and never declared or reported.
beats.say: August, Up North on Houghton Lake. Sam's boat has a forty horsepower outboard, bought two years before this policy period and never declared or reported.

beats.text: What if I hurt someone out there?
beats.say: What if I hurt someone out there?

beats.text: His 2011 HO-3 liability allows 25 horses on the back: owned outboards totaling 25 horsepower or less.
beats.say: His twenty eleven H O three liability allows twenty five horses on the back: owned outboards totaling twenty five horsepower or less.

beats.text: Bigger ones only if bought during this policy period, declared at inception, meaning when the policy began, or reported within 45 days of buying.
beats.say: Bigger ones only if bought during this policy period, declared at inception, meaning when the policy began, or reported within forty five days of buying.

beats.text: Owned sailboats 26 feet or longer? Excluded too.
beats.say: Owned sailboats twenty six feet or longer? Excluded too.

beats.text: Your call!
beats.say: Your call!

options.label: Launch it. The HO-3 covers boats!
options.fail: An owned outboard over 25 hp, owned before the policy period and never declared or reported, is excluded. No Coverage E.

beats.text: Bump! Sam's boat hits a swimmer, and she sues. No Coverage E!
beats.say: Bump! Sam's boat hits a swimmer, and she sues. No Coverage E!

options.label: Trade up to a 30-foot sailboat
options.fail: Owned sailboats 26 feet or longer are excluded too. That boat would also need the Watercraft endorsement.

beats.text: Bigger boat, same problem: it's excluded too.
beats.say: Bigger boat, same problem: it's excluded too.

options.label: Ask Dana for the Watercraft endorsement
options.win: The Watercraft endorsement adds liability coverage for the boat it describes, which the HO-3 would exclude.

beats.text: Done! Coverages E and F now apply to accidents with your boat.
beats.say: Done! Coverages E and F now apply to accidents with your boat.

reveal.text: The Watercraft endorsement adds liability for the boat it describes. It won't pay to fix the boat itself.
reveal.say: The Watercraft endorsement adds liability for the boat it describes. It won't pay to fix the boat itself.

reveal.text: Without it, neither Sam's 40-horsepower motor nor an owned 30-foot sailboat gets Coverage E.
reveal.say: Without it, neither Sam's forty horsepower motor nor an owned thirty foot sailboat gets Coverage E.

scenes.title: Jen's treasures, plus quakes and mold
scenes.src: PF&M HO 04 61 (July 2017; 2011 program); ISO HO 04 90 05 11; ISO HO 04 54 10 00; ISO HO 04 27 04 02; IRMI 'open perils'; hook mn_prop-25

draw.text: Open perils (any cause not excluded), worldwide, no deductible
New ring (2011): lesser of 25% or $10,000; report in 30 days
Except antiques, fine arts, collectibles: still ACV

beats.text: Jen schedules her jewelry. Scheduled Personal Property covers listed classes like jewelry, furs and fine arts, on open perils. That means any cause not excluded. It's worldwide, with no deductible.
beats.say: Jen schedules her jewelry. Scheduled Personal Property covers listed classes like jewelry, furs and fine arts, on open perils. That means any cause not excluded. It's worldwide, with no deductible.

beats.text: Her new ring joins that class. Under the 2011 program, think 25-10-30: 25% of the class limit or $10,000, whichever is less, if reported within 30 days.
beats.say: Her new ring joins that class. Under the twenty eleven program, think twenty five, ten, thirty: twenty five percent of the class limit or ten thousand dollars, whichever is less, if reported within thirty days.

beats.text: And Grandma's antique clock?
beats.say: And Grandma's antique clock?

beats.text: Personal Property Replacement Cost pays contents at replacement cost. But that antique clock still gets actual cash value. So do other antiques, fine arts and collectibles.
beats.say: Personal Property Replacement Cost pays contents at replacement cost. But that antique clock still gets actual cash value. So do other antiques, fine arts and collectibles.

beats.text: Earthquake, 2000 edition: shocks within 72 hours count as one quake. Mold? Limited Fungi, 2002 edition: $10,000 for property, and $50,000 as an aggregate within Coverage E.
beats.say: Earthquake, two thousand edition: shocks within seventy two hours count as one quake. Mold? Limited Fungi, two thousand two edition: ten thousand dollars for property, and fifty thousand dollars as an aggregate within Coverage E.

scenes.title: Ed strikes again: personal injury
scenes.src: PF&M 2014 (HO 24 82); ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. II Coverage E; question prop-061; memory hook mn_prop-24
scenes.plain: Not a broken bone: injury from offenses like libel, slander, false arrest, malicious prosecution, invasion of privacy, wrongful eviction or entry.
scenes.example: Ed sues Sam again, this time for slander, over something Sam told the neighbors at the block party.
scenes.exam: Coverage E pays only for bodily injury and property damage. The Personal Injury endorsement adds these offenses, but not knowingly false statements.

beats.text: You told everyone I faked my fall? That's slander!
beats.say: You told everyone I faked my fall? That's slander!

beats.text: Ed sues Sam again, this time for slander, over something Sam told the neighbors at the block party. That's personal injury, and it's not a broken bone. It's injury from offenses like libel, slander, false arrest, malicious prosecution, invasion of privacy, and wrongful eviction or entry.
beats.say: Ed sues Sam again, this time for slander, over something Sam told the neighbors at the block party. That's personal injury, and it's not a broken bone. It's injury from offenses like libel, slander, false arrest, malicious prosecution, invasion of privacy, and wrongful eviction or entry.

beats.text: Watch out: Coverage E pays only for bodily injury and property damage. Slander is neither, so no Coverage E. The Personal Injury endorsement adds these offenses, but not knowingly false statements.
beats.say: Watch out: Coverage E pays only for bodily injury and property damage. Slander is neither, so no Coverage E. The Personal Injury endorsement adds these offenses, but not knowingly false statements.

scenes.title: Work and the HO-3: who needs which add-on?
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Def. B.3, Sec. II Excl. E.2; ISO HO 04 42 10 00; PF&M 2014 (HO 24 71, HO 04 97, HO 07 01); hook mn_prop-24

spots.label: Business Pursuits
spots.text: Jen teaches for a school. This covers an insured's business activities when she isn't the owner or a partner, like teachers and salespersons.

spots.label: Permitted Incidental Occupancies
spots.text: A neighbor's piano studio at home. Covers a described business run at home, but still not bodily injury to the business's employees.

spots.label: Home Day Care Coverage
spots.text: 2011 form: paid day care for unrelated kids is a business if an occupation or paid over $2,000 in the 12 months before the policy. Excluded; this adds limited coverage.

spots.label: Home Business Insurance Coverage
spots.text: A described business run from home. A self-contained endorsement with both property and liability coverage.

beats.text: Work is a trap too: Section II excludes business liability, with a few exceptions. Tap to see who needs which endorsement.
beats.say: Work is a trap too: Section two excludes business liability, with a few exceptions. Tap to see who needs which endorsement.

reveal.text: Business Pursuits: working for someone else, like teaching. Permitted Incidental Occupancies: a described business at home, still no bodily injury to its employees.
reveal.say: Business Pursuits: working for someone else, like teaching. Permitted Incidental Occupancies: a described business at home, still no bodily injury to its employees.

reveal.text: Under the 2011 form, paid day care for unrelated kids is a business if it's an occupation, or paid over $2,000 in the 12 months before the policy period.
reveal.say: Under the twenty eleven form, paid day care for unrelated kids is a business if it's an occupation, or paid over two thousand dollars in the twelve months before the policy period.

reveal.text: Then its liability is excluded; Home Day Care Coverage adds limited coverage. Home Business Insurance Coverage: self-contained property and liability.
reveal.say: Then its liability is excluded; Home Day Care Coverage adds limited coverage. Home Business Insurance Coverage: self-contained property and liability.

scenes.q: Business Pursuits is designed to cover the work liability of which person on the Millers' street?
choices: Priya, a salesperson employed by a furniture store
Mike, a partner in a downtown law firm
Kim, the sole owner of a hardware store
scenes.why: Business Pursuits covers an insured's business activities when she isn't the owner or a partner, like salespersons and teachers.

beats.text: Quick check. Who is Business Pursuits made for?
beats.say: Quick check. Who is Business Pursuits made for?

reveal.text: Priya: she sells for an employer and isn't an owner or partner. Mike's a partner; Kim's an owner.
reveal.say: Priya: she sells for an employer and isn't an owner or partner. Mike's a partner; Kim's an owner.

scenes.title: Michigan: the innocent co-insured
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Excl. A.8; MCL 500.2833(2); Wilson (E.D. Mich. 2019); Rough Notes (March 1999); hook mn_prop-23
scenes.plain: An insured who took no part in the act that caused the loss.
scenes.example: Dan and Ana own their house together; both are insureds. Dan sets it on fire on purpose. Ana had nothing to do with it.
scenes.exam: Plain HO-3: an intentional loss bars every insured. In Michigan, an innocent co-insured is covered for a fire loss, up to her own interest.

beats.text: Down the street, Dan and Ana own a house together. Dan sets it on fire on purpose. Ana had no part in it.
beats.say: Down the street, Dan and Ana own a house together. Dan sets it on fire on purpose. Ana had no part in it.

beats.text: Both are insureds. That makes Ana an innocent co-insured: an insured who took no part in the act that caused the loss.
beats.say: Both are insureds. That makes Ana an innocent co-insured: an insured who took no part in the act that caused the loss.

beats.text: The plain HO-3 denies every insured for an intentional loss. But Michigan courts require coverage for an innocent co-insured's fire loss. She's covered up to her own interest.
beats.say: The plain H O three denies every insured for an intentional loss. But Michigan courts require coverage for an innocent co-insured's fire loss. She's covered up to her own interest.

scenes.title: Ana's call: what should she claim?
scenes.src: HO 00 03 05 11 Cond. H; MCL 500.2833(1)(q),(2); FC&S on HO 01 21 05 11 (text not seen; 05 23 may differ); prop-gap-14; IRMI 'subrogation'

beats.text: Their policy: a 2011 HO-3 with Special Provisions, Michigan. What should Ana claim?
beats.say: Their policy: a twenty eleven H O three with Special Provisions, Michigan. What should Ana claim?

options.label: Nothing. Dan's fire sinks us both.
options.fail: In Michigan, an innocent co-insured is covered for a fire loss, to the extent of her own interest.

beats.text: Ana gives up. But in Michigan, she was covered!
beats.say: Ana gives up. But in Michigan, she was covered!

options.label: The whole house, Dan's share too
options.fail: Michigan covers the innocent co-insured only to the extent of her own interest. Dan's share isn't paid.

beats.text: Not quite. Ana gets only her own interest, never Dan's share.
beats.say: Not quite. Ana gets only her own interest, never Dan's share.

options.label: Prove domestic abuse first
options.fail: Some states' versions require that. Michigan's endorsement covers the innocent co-insured with no domestic-abuse requirement.

beats.text: Wasted weeks. Michigan has no domestic-abuse test.
beats.say: Wasted weeks. Michigan has no domestic-abuse test.

options.label: Her own share of the home
options.win: Michigan's endorsement covers an innocent co-insured's fire loss to the extent of her interest, with no domestic-abuse requirement.

beats.text: Ana collects her share. Dan gets nothing, and the insurer may subrogate: go after him to recover what it paid.
beats.say: Ana collects her share. Dan gets nothing, and the insurer may subrogate: go after him to recover what it paid.

reveal.text: That's Michigan's 2011 endorsement: her own interest, no domestic-abuse test. Newer editions may differ.
reveal.say: That's Michigan's twenty eleven endorsement: her own interest, no domestic-abuse test. Newer editions may differ.

reveal.text: Suing the insurer? Ana's 2011 policy allows 2 years after the loss, tolled, meaning paused, from notice of loss until formal denial. Michigan law requires at least 1 year.
reveal.say: Suing the insurer? Ana's twenty eleven policy allows two years after the loss, tolled, meaning paused, from notice of loss until formal denial. Michigan law requires at least one year.

items: F pays others' bills, not your household's, except residence employees
E: damages plus defense, even for a groundless suit
Property of others: $1,000; not on purpose by an insured 13 or older
Boat liability the HO-3 excludes: Watercraft. Slander: Personal Injury
Michigan: innocent co-insured covered for fire, up to her interest

beats.text: F paid Ed's bills: it pays others' bills, not your household's, except residence employees. E defended Sam: damages plus defense, even for a groundless suit. On the 2011 form, property of others pays up to $1,000. But not if an insured 13 or older did it on purpose.
beats.say: F paid Ed's bills: it pays others' bills, not your household's, except residence employees. E defended Sam: damages plus defense, even for a groundless suit. On the twenty eleven form, property of others pays up to one thousand dollars. But not if an insured thirteen or older did it on purpose.

beats.text: For liability, owned boats the HO-3 excludes, like Sam's, need the Watercraft endorsement. Slander needs Personal Injury. And in Michigan, Ana got her share: an innocent co-insured is covered for a fire loss, up to her interest.
beats.say: For liability, owned boats the H O three excludes, like Sam's, need the Watercraft endorsement. Slander needs Personal Injury. And in Michigan, Ana got her share: an innocent co-insured is covered for a fire loss, up to her interest.

beats.text: Next summer? We're staying inside.
beats.say: Next summer? We're staying inside.
